plan:
- **Electronics**: ESP32 microcontroller, 2.4GHz RC receiver, brushless DC motors with ESCs for propulsion, steering servo, solar panel, MPPT charge controller, LiPo battery, waterproofing seals.
- **Mechanical**: Custom-fabricated or off-the-shelf miniature boat hull, propellers, rudder system, motor mounts, battery compartment, debris collection mechanism (e.g., scoop or net).
- **Structural**: Waterproof enclosures for electronics, internal structural supports, fasteners (screws, bolts, standoffs), watertight cable glands.
- **3D Printed Parts**: Custom mounts for solar panel, motor/servo brackets, sensor housings, debris collection scoop/net frame, controller housing for user interface.

subSteps.title: 3D print all custom parts (mounts, frames, gears, enclosure)
Clean and deburr all 3D printed parts
Prepare boat hull: Mark and drill mounting holes for internal plate, conveyor frames, debris scoop/bin, solar panel frame, and propulsion shaft components.
Install waterproof cable glands into the electronics enclosure base.
Solder motor phase wires to Left and Right Propulsion Motors.
Solder VCC and GND wires to the Conveyor Belt Motor.
Prepare power wiring: Solar Panel to MPPT, MPPT to LiPo, MPPT to PDB, PDB to ESCs, PDB to 5V Regulator.
Prepare 5V power wiring: 5V Regulator to RC Receiver, Main Controller, and Conveyor Motor Driver (VCC).
Prepare signal wiring: Main Controller to ESCs (PWM), RC Receiver to Main Controller (UART), Main Controller to Conveyor Motor Driver (GPIO).
Connect Conveyor Motor to Conveyor Motor Driver outputs.
Connect Solar Panel and LiPo battery to MPPT Charge Controller; verify charging functionality.
Power the Power Distribution Board from the MPPT; verify 5V and 12V outputs from PDB and 5V Regulator using a multimeter.
Upload basic firmware to Main Controller (main_mcu) to test GPIOs and UART communication.
Connect RC Receiver to Main Controller; verify signal reception and mapping in firmware.
Connect ESCs to Main Controller; perform initial motor calibration and test propulsion motors without propellers.
Connect Conveyor Motor Driver to Main Controller and Conveyor Motor; test basic motor function (forward/reverse).
Mount Left and Right Propulsion Motor Mounts to the Internal Mounting Plate, then attach propulsion motors to mounts.
Assemble propeller shafts: Attach shaft couplings to motor shafts, then slide shafts through bearings and seals in the boat hull, securing propellers.
Mount ESCs, Main Controller, RC Receiver, and Conveyor Motor Driver to their respective 3D printed mounts, then attach mounts to the Internal Mounting Plate.
Assemble the Conveyor Belt mechanism: Mount conveyor frames to the boat hull, attach rollers and gears, then mount the conveyor motor with its gear. Wrap conveyor belt material around rollers.
Mount the Internal Mounting Plate, Debris Scoop, Debris Storage Bin, and Solar Panel Mount Frame to the Boat Hull.
Install the Main Solar Panel onto its mount frame.
Place the LiPo Battery in its compartment and secure it with the LiPo Battery Strap.
Route all electrical cables through cable glands, tidy wiring, and secure the Electronics Enclosure Lid with the gasket to its base.

projectDescription: A miniature, solar-powered, remote-controlled boat designed for river debris collection. It features dual propulsion motors for maneuverability, a conveyor belt system to gather debris, and an integrated solar panel with MPPT charging for extended operation.

imagePromptSnapshot.description:
Project idea: miniature solar powered remote controlled river cleaning boat

Design notes: miniature, solar powered, remote controlled, river cleaning

Electrical components (current): Main Controller (mcu, 25.5x18x3.1mm); RC Receiver (module, 47x26.2x15mm); 6x actuator: Left Propulsion Motor, Right Propulsion Motor, Left Motor ESC, Right Motor ESC +2 more; 5x power: Main Solar Panel, MPPT Charge Controller, Main LiPo Battery, Power Distribution Board +1 more

Mechanical/structural parts (current): Boat Hull (enclosure, 400x150x100mm); 9x mechanism: Left Propulsion Propeller, Right Propulsion Propeller, Left Propeller Shaft Coupling, Right Propeller Shaft Coupling +5 more; 6x misc: Propeller Shaft Seal Ring, Electronics Enclosure Gasket, Waterproof Cable Gland, M3x10mm Mounting Screws +2 more; 3x 3d_printed: Main Controller Mount, RC Receiver Mount, Conveyor Motor Driver Mount

Assembly: Internal Mounting Plate → Boat Hull (M3 bolts); Debris Collection Scoop → Boat Hull (M3 bolts); Debris Storage Bin → Boat Hull (M3 bolts); Solar Panel Mount Frame → Boat Hull (M3 bolts); Electronics Enclosure Base → Internal Mounting Plate (M3 bolts); Electronics Enclosure Gasket → Electronics Enclosure Base (seated); Electronics Enclosure Lid → Electronics Enclosure Base (M3 screws); Waterproof Cable Gland → Electronics Enclosure Base (threaded connection); Left Propulsion Motor Mount → Internal Mounting Plate (M3 bolts); Right Propulsion Motor Mount → Internal Mounting Plate (M3 bolts); Left Propeller Shaft Coupling → Left Propeller Shaft (set screws); Right Propeller Shaft Coupling → Right Propeller Shaft (set screws); Left Propulsion Propeller → Left Propeller Shaft (threaded connection); Right Propulsion Propeller → Right Propeller Shaft (threaded connection); Left Propeller Shaft Bearing → Boat Hull (pressed fit/M3 bolts) (+31 more connections)

tools: Drill and drill bits (for boat hull modifications)
assumptions: Familiarity with 3D printer operation and PETG printing
Basic understanding of DC electronics and safe battery handling (LiPo)
Access to a computer with Arduino IDE or similar development environment for microcontroller programming
Ability to compile and upload firmware to the Main Controller (main_mcu)
Access to a 12V DC power supply for initial testing (optional, but recommended)
